title: Lunar eclipse crater timings, 94 eclipses 1842-2011 (Herald & Sinnott, VizieR VI/140), reduced with DE440 into the radius and shape of the Earth's shadow
verdict_rule: A shadow whose radius changes with the direction around its centre as a disc's would (its polar semi-axis |sin δ☉| of the equatorial one), or no shadow edge at all.
license_note: VizieR catalogue VI/140 (CDS), free for scientific use with citation; IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature (USGS), public domain; JPL DE440, public.

sources.cite: D. Herald and R. Sinnott, Catalogue of Lunar Eclipse Crater Timings, J. Brit. Astron. Assoc. 124 (2014) 247-253; VizieR VI/140
IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature, Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, Moon (USGS Astrogeology), feature centre points
R. S. Park, W. M. Folkner, J. G. Williams and D. H. Boggs, The JPL Planetary and Lunar Ephemerides DE440 and DE441, Astron. J. 161 (2021) 105

units.time: UT as printed (Ephemeris Time already converted by the catalogue's authors); TDB = UT + ΔT (Espenak & Meeus)
units.sigma: arcmin, angular radius of the shadow at the Moon seen from the Earth's centre
units.beta: deg, latitude on the shadow, north towards the Earth's pole of date
units.ratio: sigma divided by the median sigma of its eclipse
units.rs: km, radius of the body casting the umbra's edge, (σ + s☉)/(1/D☾ + 1/D☉) (check)

inputs.caveats: Schmidt's clocks (1842-1879) were corrected by Soulsby against modern ephemerides (doc.txt 4.5).

inputs.origin: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature (USGS), Moon feature centres.

notes: The shape (σ against the latitude on the shadow, each eclipse divided by its own median) uses angles only: a measure. The radius R_s uses the DE440 distances and a catalogue that kept only timings whose layer height, computed from the Earth's radius, lies between -50 and +250 km: a check. Schmidt's clocks (1842-1879) were corrected by Soulsby against modern ephemerides (doc.txt 4.5). Method and references: go doc -all ./internal/build/eclcrater.
public_raw_why: CDS/VizieR distributes it free for scientific use with citation; its terms do not say that a copy may be republished, so only the hash and the request are given.
